bug_semantics: CVE-2026-77081 / GHSA-jrhf-3pw6-qqwv (vendor GHSA-wcv8-x773-j96r): GraphQL node allowed-domains bypass (CWE-639). Authentication lacks noDataExpression, execute() try/catches getCredentials for every HTTP auth type, then getAllowedDomains uses the first defined credential while request assembly still attaches all loaded credential material. A workflow author can pair an unrestricted credential with a domain-restricted one, set Authentication to an expression, and send the restricted secret to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

reasoning: Re-adjudicated EVIDENCE_GAP -> NOT_AI after independent recheck (protocol-recheck-disagreements-20260829.md) and git re-verification, 2026-08-29. Basis: Git-verified by recheck (protocol-recheck-disagreements-20260829.md); adopted after review of the recheck basis. Original analysis retained for provenance: The vulnerable data flow is causal, not merely adjacent: expression mode activates multiple credential selectors; the old execution path successfully resolves all of them; the July GraphQL allowed-domains integration evaluates only the first resolved credential's policy; and later independent blocks still place material from more than one credential into the same outbound request. The aggregate parent proves the allowedDomains integration was not present immediately before the public bundle, and the public aggregate message isolates the relevant private member as GraphQL PR #208. However, protocol forbids treating a squash aggregate as the BIC. Because the private member's real commit SHA and direct parent are inaccessible, its direct-parent absence cannot be proven and its commit-object authorship/trailers cannot be judged. The August fix closes both enabling paths by forbidding expressions for Authentication and by resolving/applying only the explicitly selected credential. All three predecessor/patched tag pairs show the vulnerable-to-fixed transition exactly at the advisory's stated boundaries. The fix and lifecycle are therefore established, but a closed AI/NOT_AI verdict is not supportable without the smallest BIC object.
